title: 🏛️ Exams 2008–2025 · like + -ing, how often and the -s ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2023) A text says that Ashley cannot keep fit. Which word from the box completes the next sentence?

"She ___ eats unhealthy food."
questions.explanation: Ashley cannot keep fit because unhealthy food is what she eats every time, and the adverb that means every time is always. It stands before the verb eats. The word never would say the opposite, many is a word of quantity, and stomachache is the name of a pain: neither of them can go before a verb.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2024) A text tells what the people of a neighbourhood do every weekend. Which word from the box completes the sentence?

"We water plants and ___ paint walls."
questions.explanation: An adverb of frequency answers the question how often? and stands before the verb: and sometimes paint walls. The word but already joins ideas, so it cannot follow and, to collect is a verb form, and two verbs in a row do not make a sentence, and cleaner describes a thing, never how often we act.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025) The exam gives these words in disorder: Emma / weekends / on / walks / the / dog / usually / her. Put the groups of words in the right order to make a sentence about Emma.
questions.explanation: The sentence starts with the person, Emma. The adverb of frequency usually stands before the verb, and because Emma is she, the verb keeps its -s: walks. The activity comes next, her dog, and the time group closes the sentence: a day or the weekend takes on.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2018) John and Mary are on holiday, and it is raining. Which form completes the sentence?

"They like ___ ."
questions.explanation: After like, the activity takes the -ing form: They like swimming. The bare verb swim copies the infinitive of your own language, swims is the form that goes with he, she or it, and to swimming mixes the infinitive with the -ing form.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2013) Jane loves music. Which form completes the sentence?

"Every weekend, she ___ to the music club."
questions.explanation: Every weekend names a habit, and Jane is one girl, so she takes the -s of he, she and it: she goes. The bare verb go belongs to I, you, we and they, going cannot be the only verb of the sentence, and to go is an infinitive.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2010) It is Sunday afternoon and Jane is going to the zoo with her family. Which word from the box completes the sentence?

"She ___ rabbits."
questions.explanation: Jane is one girl, so she is she, and the verb like takes an -s: she likes rabbits. The form like forgets that -s. The words plays and is come from the same box, but they do not say what she feels about rabbits.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2010) Today is a holiday. Which word completes the sentence?

"It's eleven o'clock ___ the morning."
questions.explanation: The morning is only a part of the day, with no day named beside it, so it takes in: in the morning. The word on is kept for a day (on Monday morning), and at and of do not go with the morning.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2009) The exam gives these words in disorder: eating / Children / sandwiches / like. Put them in the right order to make a sentence.
questions.explanation: The people come first, Children, and then the verb like. After like the activity takes the -ing form: eating, and what they eat closes the sentence: sandwiches.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2008) The exam gives these words in disorder: guitar / likes / playing / the / Alex. Put the groups of words in the right order to make a sentence.
questions.explanation: Alex is one boy, so he is he and the verb like takes its -s: Alex likes. After likes, the activity takes the -ing form: playing, and the thing he plays closes the sentence: the guitar.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2008) The exam gives these words in disorder: zoo / on / go / the / Sundays / to / I. Put the groups of words in the right order to make a sentence.
questions.explanation: The sentence starts with the person and the verb, I go to, and the place follows: the zoo. The time group closes it, and a day takes on: on Sundays.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2017) Tommy is from France. Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Tommy is one boy, so he is he, and the present simple verb takes an -s: he lives. The form live forgets that -s, living has no be in front of it, and is live puts be before a bare verb.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015) A boy tells what he does in the morning. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I drink usually milk or juice.
I usually drinking milk or juice.
I usually drink milk or juice.
I usually drinks milk or juice.

questions.explanation: The adverb of frequency usually stands before the verb: I usually drink. With I the verb stays in its bare form. Putting usually after the verb breaks that rule, drinking is an -ing form with no be before it, and drinks takes the -s of he, she and it.
